podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Forming First Band (1976)
podcast.body: At 16 in 1976, after moving back to Australia, he joined a band possibly called Dr. Dolphin with school friends Andrew Ferris (keyboards) and Gary Beers (bass), who remained his bandmates for life. His poetry was highly regarded, making him the group's lyricist. "In 1976, when he was 16 and after the family moved back to Australia, he fell in with a trio of school friends in a band that may have been called Dr. Dolphin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Meeting with Paula Yates (1985)
podcast.body: As a guest on the British TV show *The Tube* in 1985, he met host Paula Yates, then partnered with Bob Geldof. He immediately asked her to return to his hotel room; she declined, but a strong connection was established, potentially initiating an affair. "In 1985, Hutchins was a guest on the British TV show The Tube. The host was Paula Yates, and she, for the last 10 years, had been with Bob Geldoff, he of the Bumpton Rats and the organizer of Live Aid."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Acting Debut (1986)
podcast.body: In 1986, he ventured into acting, appearing in the film *Dogs in Space*. "In 1986, he made a detour into acting, appearing in a film called Dogs in Space."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Copenhagen Assault and Head Injury (August 1992)
podcast.body: In August 1992, he was assaulted by a cab driver in Copenhagen, hitting his head on a curb and fracturing his skull. The injury resulted in the permanent loss of his senses of smell and taste, leading to depression, increased aggression, and physical altercations with band members, including one instance where he pulled a knife. "In August 1992, Michael was assaulted by a cab driver in Copenhagen. He was shoved and ended up hitting his head on the curb, fracturing his skull, and the injuries resulted in him permanently losing his senses of smell and taste."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Copenhagen Assault and Irreversible Brain Damage (August 1992)
podcast.body: While touring Copenhagen with girlfriend Helena Christensen, Hutchence was sucker-punched by an impatient taxi driver, causing him to fall and hit his head violently on the curb. Although paramedics initially assumed he was on drugs, he sustained severe, irreversible brain damage, which fundamentally altered his personality. "The blow to the head brought something out of Michael and it ended up killing him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Injury Personality Change and Aggression (1992-1997)
podcast.body: Following his brain injury, the previously quiet and gentle Hutchence became aggressive, erratic, and quick to fight, suffering from headaches, vomiting, and a destroyed sense of taste and smell. This change led to rages where he destroyed furniture, damaged a valuable guitar owned by Andrew Farriss, and even threatened bassist Gary Beers with a knife in the studio. "From that point on, the quiet, gentle Michael Hutchins was suddenly different."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Confrontation with Prince (1994)
podcast.body: At the World Music Awards in Monaco in 1994, Hutchence, whose behavior was worsening due to increasing drug and alcohol use stemming from his brain injury, attempted to pick a fight with Prince. "And at the World Music Awards in Monaco in 1994, he tried to pick a fight with Prince."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Quote on Pop and Suicide (1994)
podcast.body: In 1994, not long after Kurt Cobain's suicide, Hutchence commented on self-harm and the music industry's destructive nature, stating, "people killing themselves over stuff they shouldn't. Pop eats its young, that's for sure." "people killing themselves over stuff they shouldn't. Pop eats its young, that's for sure."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Big Breakfast Interview (1994)
podcast.body: In 1994, he reunited with Paula Yates on her show *The Big Breakfast* for a seven-minute interview conducted on a bed, with both entwined. The media widely labeled it "the most sexually charged TV interview of all time," and it was watched by two million people. During the interview, he discussed a greatest hits album, ending a contract with an American record company, and scaling back his clubbing habits. "In 1994, they met again for Paula's new show The Big Breakfast. As soon as it was over, the media was calling that interview the most sexually charged TV interview of all time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relationship with Paula Yates and Tabloid Coverage (1995-1997)
podcast.body: Hutchence was involved in a complex and unhealthy breakup with British TV personality Paula Yates, the mother of his children, by 1995. Their relationship was characterized by extensive drug and alcohol use and became a prominent subject of tabloid coverage. "By 1995, he was locked into a complex breakup with Paula Yates, the British TV person."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Split from Helena Christensen (March 1995)
podcast.body: He separated from Helena Christensen in March 1995 after being discovered with Paula Yates in a hotel, a development that became a major tabloid sensation in England. "Hutchinson, Christianson, split up after he was caught with Yates in a hotel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Chelsea Drug Raid (September 1996)
podcast.body: In September 1996, he was implicated in a drug raid at Paula Yates's Chelsea home, where opium and smoking pipes were found. Both he and Yates claimed the drugs had been planted by employees. "Michael and Paula responded by saying that the drugs were planted."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Date of Death (November 22, 1997)
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence died on November 22, 1997. "Michael Hutchins died on November 22, 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death (November 1997)
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence, identified as "Michael Hutchins" and the singer of "in excess," died in November 1997 by hanging. "Michael Hutchins, singer, in excess, death by hanging for some reason, November 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death Location (November 22, 1997)
podcast.body: His body was discovered in Room 524 of the Ritz Carlton Hotel in Sydney. "his body was found in room 524 of the Ritz Carlton Hotel in Sydney."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death at Ritz Carlton (November 22-23, 1997)
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence met his end in room 524 of the Ritz Carlton in Sydney, Australia. On the night of November 22nd, 1997, after filming a TV special for INXS's 20th anniversary and having dinner, he returned to his suite. Following late-night visitors, he made phone calls, then appeared "really rough" at the front desk. Back in his room, he apparently went into a rage, trashing the room, throwing prescription pills, and breaking his hand. Sometime between 9:50 am and 10:30 am on November 23rd, 1997, he fastened a leather belt to a doorknob and hanged himself. He was found by a maid at 11:50 am. The most popular verdict was auto-erotic asphyxiation, and he was 37 years old. "Michael Hutchins met his end in room 524 of the Ritz Carlton in Sydney, Australia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death at Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel (November 22-23, 1997)
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence's final hours began after dinner with his father and stepmother in Sydney on November 22, 1997, where he subsequently returned to room 524 at the Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel. He had champagne, daiquiris, and beer with his ex-girlfriend Kim Wilson and her current boyfriend in the hotel bar, continuing to his room for a nightcap. After they left at 4 AM, he made several unanswered phone calls to ex-girlfriends. Early on November 23rd, he mailed some letters, appearing "pretty rough" to the clerk. Housekeeping discovered him dead around noon, the room in disarray with prescription pills scattered and furniture moved. He died between 9:50 and 10:30 AM, having been strangled by a belt hung on a door. His cause of death has been debated, with official findings concluding auto-erotic asphyxiation, though suicide was also considered, despite no note. "Michael was dead. He had been strangled by a belt hung on a door."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death at Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel (November 22-23, 1997)
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence met his end in room 524 of the Ritz Carlton in Sydney, Australia. Sometime between 9:50 am and 10:30 am on November 23rd, 1997, he fastened a leather belt to a doorknob and hanged himself. He was found by a maid at 11:50 am. The most popular verdict was auto-erotic asphyxiation, and he was 37 years old. "Michael Hutchins met his end in room 524 of the Ritz Carlton in Sydney, Australia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Apparent Suicide (November 22, 1997)
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence was found dead in a Sydney hotel room on November 22, 1997, in what was apparently a suicide. Those close to him believe his death was ultimately a consequence of the brain injury he suffered five years prior in Copenhagen. "on November 22, 1997, Hutchins was found dead in a Sydney hotel room, apparently by suicide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Paranoia and Mental State (1997)
podcast.body: In early 1997, amidst wedding plans with Paula Yates, he became increasingly paranoid, believing his phones and homes were bugged. During promo and final tours that year, he appeared tired, older than his 37 years, and exhibited erratic behavior during shows. "He had become paranoid, claiming that his phones and houses were bugged."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Psychiatric Consultation (October 17, 1997)
podcast.body: On October 17, 1997, he consulted London psychiatrist Mark Collins for what he described as "minor depression." Collins reported no signs of suicidal ideation at that time. "He did see a London psychiatrist named Mark Collins on October 17, 1997, regarding what he termed to be a minor depression. Collins said there was no sign of any suicidal thoughts on that date."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Autopsy Results
podcast.body: His autopsy revealed his blood contained alcohol, cocaine, Prozac, and various prescription drugs. He was determined to have been paranoid, depressed, and acting erratically. "an autopsy show that Hutchins blood was filled with alcohol, cocaine, prozac and a few prescription drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Brain Tumor Theory
podcast.body: A theory emerged that he was convinced he had a brain tumor and intended to commit suicide before the tumor could kill him, similar to Kurt Cobain's reported stomach issues. Cat scans disproved the tumor, but a friend recalled Hutchence stating he "would do a curt before the cancer got to him." "Another theory was that Michael was convinced he had a brain tumor and he was going to kill himself before the tumor did."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Charisma and Frontman Status
podcast.body: He evolved into a major star, described as handsome, charismatic, a rich rock star with immense sexual energy, and a genuinely amazing frontman. "He had been transformed into a major star. And why not? Handsome, charismatic. He was a rich rock star with sexual energy to burn. And he was a legitimately amazing frontman."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cremation and Ash Dispute
podcast.body: Following his cremation, a significant dispute arose over his ashes involving his family, Paula Yates, and the band. "And later when Michael was cremated, there was a big fight over his ashes between his family, Paula, and the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death Circumstances
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence died during what was described as a "weird auto-erotic asphyxiation thing gone wrong." "And then of course, Michael died during some weird auto-erotic asphyxiation thing gone wrong."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rock Star Kids ｜ From the Archives

podcast.title: Discovery of Body (10:50 AM, November 22)
podcast.body: His naked body was found at 10:50 AM, kneeling and facing the door, with his head strained into a broken belt loop. No suicide note was present. "At 10.50 a.m., his body was found. Michael was naked in a kneeling position facing the door. His head was strained so far forward into the loop of the belt that the buckle had broken. There was no suicide note."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Influences
podcast.body: Son of an Australian wine importer and a socialite, he grew up in Sydney, Brisbane, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, and the Bronx, which contributed to his distinctive accent. Initially a promising swimmer, a badly broken arm ended that path, leading him to poetry and later a singing job at a Hong Kong toy store. "Michael grew up in Sydney, Brisbane, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, even the Bronx."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Father of Heavenly Hiraani Tiger Lily Hutchence
podcast.body: Michael Hutchence of INXS had a daughter named Heavenly Hiraani Tiger Lily with British TV host Paula Yates. "They had a daughter named Heavenly, Heranny Tiger Lily."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rock Star Kids ｜ From the Archives

podcast.title: Fatherhood and Custody Strain
podcast.body: He became a father to Heavenly Hiraani Tiger Lily with Paula Yates. Despite his pride in fatherhood, he was caught in the midst of the contentious custody battle between Yates and Bob Geldof, a strain that worsened his addictions and existing predilections. "Michael and Paula were the parents of a baby girl named Heveli, Herani, Tiger Lily. And while he was proud to be a father, Michael was caught in the middle of everything between Paula and Bob."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Final Messages to Managers
podcast.body: On the morning of his death, he left voicemail messages for his personal manager, Martha Troup, at 9:38 AM and 9:50 AM. Separately, his tour manager, John Martin, received a note from Hutchence indicating he would miss an important rehearsal that day. "At 9.38 a.m., he left a voice mill for Martha Troop, his personal manager."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Final Violent Outburst and Method of Death
podcast.body: In a state described as depressed, drunk, stoned, and exhausted, he experienced a violent rage in his hotel room between 9:50 AM and 10:30 AM, scattering five types of prescription pills, breaking his hand by punching a wall, and cutting his face while throwing furniture. During this period, he used a snakeskin leather belt, fastened to a door, to hang himself. "Apparently, depressed, drunk, stoned, exhausted, Michael went into some kind of violent rage in the room, scattering five different types of prescription pills all over the place, and breaking his hand when he punched the wall, oh and throwing some of the furniture around cutting up his face in the process."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Financial Status and Estate
podcast.body: Despite InXS's extensive album sales and his profitable investment in the film *Crocodile Dundee*, Hutchence had been facing severe money problems for years and was "practically bankrupt" at the time of his death. Although a complex series of trusts and holding companies held at least eight million pounds, legal fees left "virtually nothing left" in his estate years later. "But as it turns out, Michael had been having money problems for years and was practically bankrupt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Funeral (November 27)
podcast.body: His funeral was held on November 27 and broadcast live on TV across Australia. "His funeral was on November 27th and was carried live on TV across Australia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Funeral Incidents
podcast.body: His funeral was disrupted by a "hysterical fan" known for intentionally ruining public events, who screamed obscenities and threatened to hang himself from the church balcony. "Meanwhile, a hysterical fan showed up, started screaming obscenities and threatened to hang himself from the balcony of the church."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: International Media Coverage of Death
podcast.body: Hutchence's death was a national news event in Australia for months and became a major tabloid story in the UK due to his connections. In North America, coverage was less extensive, partly because InXS's peak years had passed and the Bill Clinton-Monica Lewinsky scandal dominated headlines. "His death was national news in Australia for months."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Last Call with Bob Geldof
podcast.body: Between 4 AM and 5 AM on the day of his death, he made two calls to Bob Geldof, engaging in a loud, 20-minute argument. He attempted to persuade Geldof to lift an injunction against Paula Yates, allowing the children to come to Australia for Christmas, but Geldof refused. Hutchence was heard screaming phrases like, "your children hate you. I'm their father, little man." "Hutchins called Bob Geldoff twice. Michael wanted to persuade Bob to drop the cordon junction against Paula and let the three kids come to Australia for Christmas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Last Call with Michelle Bennett (9:54 AM, November 22)
podcast.body: At 9:54 AM on November 22, he spoke with ex-girlfriend Michelle Bennett, who reported he sounded "crying and depressed and sounded drunk." She promptly drove to the hotel, attempted to call his room (524) from the lobby, and then knocked on his door around 10:40 AM, but received no answer, subsequently leaving a note at reception. "At 9.54 a.m., this is November 22nd, she did answer. She says that Michael was crying and depressed and sounded drunk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Last Dinner
podcast.body: The day before his death, he had dinner with his father and stepmother at the Flavor of India restaurant in Sydney. He appeared normal, laughing and joking, but his father sensed something was amiss. "Afterwards Michael went out for dinner with his father and stepmother at a restaurant called Flavor of India."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Last Hours and Party
podcast.body: After dinner on November 21, around 10:30 PM, he returned to Room 524 of the Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel. He engaged in a "last bender" with ex-girlfriend Kim Wilson, an Australian soap opera star, and her boyfriend, consuming daiquiris, champagne, and beer in the hotel bar before going to his room. The couple departed the hotel around 4 AM on November 22. "He called up Kim Wilson, an Australian soap opera star and ex-girlfriend. She and her boyfriend came to the hotel where they banged back a bunch of daiquiri, champagne and beer in the hotel bar before going out to Michael's room."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Last Phone Call with Paula Yates (5:38 AM, November 22)
podcast.body: At 5:38 AM on November 22, Paula Yates called him and later described him as sounding "really desperate." "At 5.38 a.m., Paula called. Three later said that Michael sounded really desperate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mailing Last Letters
podcast.body: Early on the morning of his death, looking "really rough," he visited the hotel front desk to ask a clerk to mail two letters: one addressed to Paula Yates and another to a friend in Hong Kong. This was the last time anyone saw him alive. "Early in the morning and looking really rough, he went on to the front desk and asked the clerk to mail two letters that he had written. One to Paula and the other to a friend in Hong Kong."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Official Cause of Death and Alternative Theories
podcast.body: His death on November 22, 1997, was officially ruled a suicide. However, in 1999, Paula Yates suggested on *60 Minutes* Australia that he died from auto-erotic asphyxiation gone wrong, a theory the coroner explicitly rejected due to lack of forensic evidence. This theory gained widespread belief, fueled by Hutchence's known sexual kinks, his mother's mention of him being with sadomasochists, and his own comments about seeking the "ultimate sexual high." "Again, the corner rule that Michael Hutchins died by his own hand in that hotel room on November 22, 1997. But then in 1999, Paula Yates made a suggestion. Totally contrary to everything she'd said up until that point. On the Australian version of 60 minutes, she intimated that Michael may have died as the result of solo sex play gone wrong. Auto-erotic asphyxiation, which he took too far."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Party Lifestyle and Tabloid Nickname
podcast.body: Known for heavy party drug use (cocaine, ecstasy, methadone, alcohol), frequenting fashionable nightclubs, open drug use, and drunken brawls. This behavior earned him the British tabloid nickname "the Wild Man of Rock." "Some of the British tabloids started calling him the Wild Man of Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Posthumous Works and Legacy
podcast.body: Numerous books, biographies, and at least two major documentaries, *Michael Hutchence: The Last Rock and Roll Star* (2017) and *Mystify Michael Hutchence* (2019), have been released about him. Despite these, unanswered questions about his death persist. His legacy positions him as one of rock's greatest frontmen, and it is suggested InXS would likely be a successful heritage band touring today if he were alive. "There were half a dozen books in biographies, and there have been at least two major documentaries. Michael Hutchinson's The Last Rock and Roll Star in 2017, and mystified Michael Hutchinson's in 2019."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominent Relationships (Unspecified Period)
podcast.body: During his lifetime, Michael Hutchence was consistently seen with highly prominent and beautiful women, including film director Michelle Bennett, singer Kylie Minogue, and supermodel Helena Christensen. He also had a relationship with Australian soap opera star Kim Wilson, who was the inspiration for an INXS song. "When he was alive, he was always in the company of some of the most beautiful women in the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Public Mourning and Funeral Service
podcast.body: His funeral service at St Andrew's Cathedral was a widely observed event, with public mourning across Australia and globally for a figure who felt intimately connected to fans. An InXS song prominently featured in the service. "This in excess song featured prominently in the service at St Andrews Cathedral."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relationship with Helena Christensen
podcast.body: After his relationship with Kylie Minogue ended, he married supermodel Helena Christensen. They resided in a lavish house on five acres in the south of France, where they hosted renowned and beautiful guests from around the world. "Supermodel Helena Christensen entered the picture. They got married and lived in an incredible house on five acres in the south of France, where they entertained famous and beautiful people from all over the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relationship with Kylie Minogue
podcast.body: His relationship with Kylie Minogue transformed her public image from a "mild-mannered pop star" to a "supervixen dude." He openly stated his hobby was "corrupting her." Tabloids frequently reported on their relationship, including stories about customs finding handcuffs and other devices in her luggage, all-night ecstasy binges, and embarrassing nightclub moments. Kylie was also allegedly the inspiration for a song after expressing a desire to dye her hair. "Michael even admitted that his hobby was, quote, corrupting her."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relationships and Early Promiscuity
podcast.body: He was known for dating some of the world's most beautiful women, making him a tabloid favorite. His partners included Virginia Hey (a Bond girl), Belinda Carlisle (The Go-Go's singer), and Kylie Minogue. From the age of 15, women were a "real weakness," with early touring days sometimes involving sex with three women a night in the band's panel van. "He went out with Virginia Hay, a bond girl from the living daylights. He went out with Blinda Carlyle, the singer of the Go-Gos. Singer Kylie Minogue was a partner for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Wedding Plans with Paula Yates
podcast.body: He and Paula Yates were planning to marry in Tahiti as soon as they could find the time. "They were going to get married in Tahiti just as soon as the two of them could find the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
